newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Moslem vigilantes promise to keep peace.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Moslem vigilantes promise to keep peace.

text.p: South African Moslem vigilantes who publicly executed a drug dealer three months ago made a promise to police on Friday to obey the law in future and spare Cape Town further scenes of unrest and violence.

The Moslem group, called People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad), made headlines in August when a mob of its supporters tracked down a known drug dealer, shot him in the head and set his body on fire in full view of television cameras in Cape Town.
Earlier this month, a Pagad member was shot dead when police opened fire to prevent a demonstration by the vigilante group getting out of control.
"Pagad undertook that their gatherings will be peaceful and within the ambit of the law," the Moslem group's leaders and the police said in a joint statement after meeting to broker a truce.
In a separate statement, Pagad said the pledge did not mean the end to their campaign against gangs and drugs.
Pagad has also come under fire from religious leaders and academics for urging Moslems to arm themselves against President Nelson Mandela's government.

"We are deeply concerned at the level of militancy that is being displayed by Pagad (and) its confrontational and intolerant approach in public, which puts ordinary citizens at risk," Cape Town clerics said in a recent statement.
